A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MUSYC survey is a powerful tool for studying galaxy formation and evolution at z ∼2.

the BzK galaxies at z ∝ 2 are massive, luminous, and clustered galaxies that are forming stars at rates of 20–100 M☉ yr-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at a given redshift, the clustering properties of BzK galaxies are independent of their star formation activity.
, in the absence of spectroscopic redshifts, BzK selection is a robust method of identifying star-forming and passively evolving galaxies over a large area of the sky.
BzK galaxies are not strongly clustered, but rather they are found in a variety of environments, ranging from the outskirts of rich clusters to the field.
